scope: learned versus classical undersampled multi-echo GRE reconstruction, compared through downstream R2* and B0 ROI measurements
compute: CPU only (no GPU). Training of the learned reconstruction should take minutes, not hours.

inputs.inputs/train.npz: kspace complex64 [180, 5, 64, 64] fully sampled (noisy) k-space of 30 training subjects x 6 slices; labels int16 [180, 64, 64]; subject_id str [180]; slice_index int [180]; te_s float [5]
inputs.inputs/test.npz: kspace complex64 [32, 5, 64, 64] undersampled k-space (zeros where not sampled) of 8 test subjects x 4 slices; mask bool [32, 5, 64, 64] (True = sampled); labels; subject_id; slice_index; te_s. No fully sampled data or truth is provided for test subjects.

conventions.fft: k = fftshift(fft2(ifftshift(img, axes=(-2,-1)), norm='ortho'), axes=(-2,-1)) and img = fftshift(ifft2(ifftshift(k, axes=(-2,-1)), norm='ortho'), axes=(-2,-1)) (numpy). Axis -2 = y (rows), axis -1 = x (columns). Single receive coil.
conventions.acquisition: 5-echo spoiled GRE, TE = 4.0, 9.9, 15.8, 21.7, 27.6 ms (te_s). Each 64x64 k-space is the phase-encode plane of a 3D acquisition and is undersampled in 2D.
conventions.sampling: Independently for every slice and echo: all k-space points within radius 5.5 (in samples) of the centre (index 32, 32) are sampled; the remaining samples are drawn without replacement with probability proportional to 1/(1 + (r/8)^2), r = distance from the centre in samples, for a total of 1024 samples per echo (acceleration 4). Masks of the test and hidden data follow this distribution; use the supplied mask of each case.
conventions.noise: complex Gaussian, standard deviation 0.018 per real/imaginary channel in k-space (orthonormal FFT, so the same in image space)
conventions.signal_model: S_n(r) = PD(r) exp(-R2*(r) TE_n) exp(i (phi0(r) + 2 pi dB0(r) TE_n)) inside the object (labels > 0), zero outside; phi0 is a smooth background phase, |dB0| < 75 Hz
conventions.labels: 0 background, 1 white-matter-like, 2 deep grey, 3 cortex-like rim, 4 focal lesions with high R2*

downstream_definition.r2s: voxelwise weighted log-linear fit of ln|S_n| = ln S0 - R2* TE_n with weights |S_n|^2 over all 5 echoes; R2* in 1/s
downstream_definition.b0: voxelwise dB0 = angle( sum_{n=1..4} S_{n+1} conj(S_n) ) / (2 pi dTE), dTE = 5.9 ms; in Hz
downstream_definition.roi: for each slice and label k in {1,2,3,4}: ROI = one-voxel binary erosion of (labels == k) (scipy.ndimage.binary_erosion default 3x3 cross); the ROI is used only if it has >= 10 voxels; ROI value = mean of the voxelwise R2* (or dB0) over the ROI
downstream_definition.error_metrics: relative R2* error |R2*_roi / R2*_ref - 1| and absolute dB0 error |dB0_roi - dB0_ref| (Hz) pooled over all used (slice, label) ROIs; summarised by the median and the 90th percentile

requirements.split: Split the training subjects into training and validation sets BY SUBJECT (no subject in both; at least 3 validation subjects). Use validation subjects (with masks you draw from the stated distribution) for model selection, tuning of the classical method and the method comparison; the reference for validation is the downstream analysis of the fully sampled validation images.
requirements.learned: a reconstruction network trained by you on CPU from train.npz
requirements.classical: a non-learned reconstruction (for example compressed sensing) with its regularisation tuned on the validation subjects
requirements.fairness: both methods reconstruct identical test data with the identical supplied masks
requirements.outputs_scale: returned images are in the image space defined by the FFT convention, at the same intensity scale and orientation (no normalisation, flips or shifts)

entrypoints.predict.py: python predict.py --input <archive.npz> --output <recon.npz>: learned reconstruction from an archive with the schema of test.npz; uses only code and saved weights in its own folder (it is run with that folder as working directory)
entrypoints.classical_recon.py: python classical_recon.py --input <archive.npz> --output <recon.npz>: the tuned classical reconstruction, same interface
entrypoints.rerun: Both entrypoints are rerun on hidden test subjects (same protocol and mask distribution, new masks).

downstream_results.json.validation: {subjects: [...], learned: {...}, classical: {...}, zero_filled: {...}} where each method has r2s_rel_err_median, r2s_rel_err_p90, b0_abs_err_median_hz, b0_abs_err_p90_hz (and optionally image metrics) measured on the validation subjects against the fully sampled reference
downstream_results.json.classical_tuning: {parameter: str, values: [tried values], selected: value, criterion: str}
downstream_results.json.test: {learned: [...], classical: [...]}: for each test case in test.npz order an object mapping each used label ("1".."4") to {r2s_per_s, b0_hz} computed with the downstream definition from your reconstruction
downstream_results.json.preferred_method: "learned" or "classical" for this downstream task, with preferred_rationale

required_outputs.figure: a .png comparing zero-filled, learned and classical images and R2* maps
required_outputs.code: training script, network definition, saved weights, predict.py, classical_recon.py and evaluation scripts
required_outputs.README.md: methods, validation evidence and a section titled Limitations

file_locations: Deliverables in the workspace root or one subfolder; each requested file must exist exactly once.
grading_note: The grader recomputes the downstream analysis from your test reconstructions and compares it with the ground-truth R2* and dB0 maps (expected for EACH method: R2* relative error median <= 3.5 % and 90th percentile <= 11 %; dB0 error median <= 0.5 Hz and 90th percentile <= 1.5 Hz; zero filling does not meet these), checks the k-space residual of each reconstruction at the sampled locations (<= 0.35 of the measured norm), checks that your reported test ROI values match your reconstructions, checks the split, and reruns both entrypoints on hidden subjects.
